findings.title: hasPermission(String) looks up resource with swapped name/id arguments, likely always failing
findings.body: In `hasPermission(String scope)`, `resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId())` passes the resource server's id as the owner argument. Compare with `getOrCreateResource`/`hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` which use `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` differently, and with `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource` which does a plain `findByName(resourceServer, type.getType())` without an owner. If the `findByName(ResourceServer, String name, String owner)` overload actually requires the resource owner (not server id) to match the stored resource's owner, this lookup can fail to find the all-clients resource (created with `resourceServer.getClientId()` as owner in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`), causing `canManageClientScopes()`/`canView(ClientScopeModel)` to always return false even when an all-clients permission exists. This diverges from the correct pattern used elsewhere (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource`), and should use the same consistent lookup rather than owner=server.getId().

findings.title: Mismatched resource lookup key in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) vs. resource creation
findings.body: `hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` looks up `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`, using the client's internal id as resource name. But resources for individual clients are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` using `name = resolveClient(session, id)` which resolves to `client.getId()` as well, so this should match — however the owner parameter passed is `server.getId()` whereas resources are created with owner `resourceServer.getClientId()` (see `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())`). If `server.getId()` differs from `resourceServer.getClientId()` (likely, since one is the resource-server's internal id, the other is the owning client's id), this lookup will never find existing per-client resources, breaking the per-client manage/view/configure checks and effectively relying only on the all-clients fallback path.

findings.title: Potential NPE when all-clients resource type is not yet created
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client resource is not found, the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` which can return null (e.g., if resource type resource was never created, or `supportsAuthorizationSchema` returns false). The result is then passed directly into `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` without a null check, risking an NPE instead of gracefully returning false.
